heading: What each realm refuses
body:
Every annotation above appears in each language that accepts it. The missing examples are not mistakes. The compiler rejects these combinations before anything runs, and its error message says why.

A native Tac service is a Swift, Kotlin, C# or Rust service that Tachyon links into a native companion. It carries the Service marker like every class in client/services (TY1363). It accepts Service, Lifetime, NeedsAll, Needs, Named, the data and behavior annotations, Setup, CacheSettings, Entity, Table, Store, Checked, Settings, WhenProfile, WhenSetting and HTTPClient. A native companion has no page storage and no page transport, so its Setup names every cache and entity adapter that the service uses, and the native build stops when one is missing (ADR 0059). Its HTTPClient sends requests through the HTTP adapter that its Setup names. A native Rust service injects a Helper with Needs, and a native C# service builds one with `new`; Swift and Kotlin refuse Helper with TY1308. A linked native service cannot use page-only APIs such as PreferenceStrings and DocumentTitle. It receives the native WindowControls and FilePicker providers instead (ADR 0089; see Native services). StreamRequest and SocketRequest clients are written in JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Ruby, Rust or Dart; the page's JavaScript holds the connection for a Go, Ruby, Rust or Dart service. A client in any other Tac language fails with TY1308 at the client file, and the message names its language, for example `@StreamRequest is not available in Java Tac code`, or `[<SocketRequest>] is not available in F# Tac code` in F#.

Lua, Python and C++ are Tac service languages with limits. This table lists what each one refuses.

| Language | What the build refuses in Tac code |
| --- | --- |
| Lua (ADR 0085) | TY1308 for the behavior annotations (Setup, Settings, Setting, WhenProfile, WhenSetting, CacheSettings, Cached, ClearCache, UpdateCache, Retry, MaxAtOnce, AllOrNothing, Checked, Check and the field checks), Entity, Store, Query, HTTPClient and its request annotations, LocalState, SessionState, Helper, Fake, TestSettings and FreshStart. Lua has no WindowControls. TY2015 for a Needs field whose type is another service. It accepts Service, Lifetime, Needs, Named, NeedsAll, OnStart, OnStop, OnEvent, Order, InBackground, Topic, Converter, Convert, Test, TestSetup, UseProfiles and ValueSource. |
| Python (ADR 0093) | TY1605 for `async def` methods, streams and the browser API resources. TY1308 for Store, Query, HTTPClient and its request annotations, ValueSource, LocalState, SessionState, the caching annotations, PageDefaults, Retry, MaxAtOnce and AllOrNothing. A Python Check cannot read a Checked model from client/models yet (TY1308), and a Python Needs field cannot name a Converter yet (TY1605). Python accepts Service, Lifetime, Needs, Named, NeedsAll, Helper, synchronous OnStart, OnStop and OnEvent with their options, ApplicationEventPublisher, Topic, Test, TestSetup and UseProfiles. |
| C++ (ADR 0099) | TY1308 for every annotation that C++ does not reach yet, such as Setup, the behavior annotations, Entity, Store, Query, LocalState, SessionState, Topic, Helper, Converter, Lifetime, Named and NeedsAll. TY1372 for a `Needs` field that names anything but a C++ service or a C++ HTTPClient, so C++ has no browser APIs yet. TY1371 for a file that is not one header-only class, and for a lowercase marker such as `[[service]]`. C++ accepts Service, Needs, OnStart, OnStop, OnEvent, Order, InBackground, ApplicationEventPublisher, HTTPClient with its request annotations, Test, TestSetup, Fake and ValueSource. |

Other languages refuse fewer annotations. Swift, Kotlin, Ruby and Java refuse Helper with TY1308. A Go Helper belongs to the service that needs or creates it, so it has no Needs, NeedsAll, Lifetime or lifecycle hooks of its own; the build stops those with TY1308 or TY1405. A Java service cannot ask for another service with Needs, and it cannot use Named; the build stops both with TY1405. A Ruby service cannot ask for another service with Needs either; the build stops it with TY2015 (ADR 0054).

The build also checks where each annotation is written (ADR 0056). It refuses an annotation on the wrong kind of member, such as Cached on a field. It refuses arguments on an annotation that takes none, such as Service, and a missing argument list on one that needs it, such as Test or Named. It refuses an annotation that needs an instance method, such as a route, a listener or Cached, on a static method, the same annotation twice on one member, and two annotations that clash, such as LocalState with SessionState, or Cached with ClearCache. It refuses an annotation without its partner: Order or InBackground without OnEvent, Named without Needs, Id outside an Entity class, and Fake or ValueSource outside a Test or TestSetup class. NeedsAll takes no field list, and a NeedsAll class declares no constructor. Each message names the annotation in your language's spelling, the member, the right place and what the annotation means. These refusals use TY1308.

InBackground listeners (methods that run when an event happens) need a language whose methods can be asynchronous. In Yon, these languages are JavaScript, TypeScript and Python. PHP, Java, Groovy, Kotlin, C#, F#, Rust, Dart, Go, Ruby and Lua reject the annotation. They do not pretend to delay the call. Tac accepts InBackground in every service language that has listeners, because it only delays delivery on the page.

A StreamRoute method (ADR 0058; the old `@Stream` name is retired) returns its values one at a time, so the language needs a way to do that. JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, PHP, Kotlin, C#, F#, Dart and Ruby use their own generator syntax, Lua sends each value with `coroutine.yield`, and Go returns an `iter.Seq` (Go's range-over-function iterator). Java, Groovy and Rust refuse StreamRoute. They return the whole collection at once.

Both realms refuse a field that Tachyon fills, a Needs field or a NeedsAll field without a starting value, when it is declared nullable. Tachyon never leaves such a field null, so `label?: string` or `final String? path;` would only mislead the reader. The build stops with TY1331 and shows the non-null form to write instead. Both realms also refuse, with TY1332, a field that holds an injected class and does not use the language's variable case, such as `CartStore CartStore;` in Java or `cartStore` in Python.

Gateway exists only in Yon. A Tac service has no supervisor that could start another language for one call. So the annotation fails with TY1308 in every Tac language. Public, SignedIn, Allow and IdentityProvider exist only in Yon, because only a server can decide who may call a route. A Tac page cannot protect data: the server route must say who may call it.
